name: Roasted Chestnut & Herb Pesto Pasta with Mushrooms
why: Chestnut season is peaking right now, and this one-pan pasta turns 100g of them into a vibrant green-herb pesto that coats the whole bowl. A 25-minute weeknight dinner with real autumn personality — no cream, no fuss.
author: Henry
ingredients: A handful each of basil, parsley and mint, leaves only
50g parmesan, grated, plus extra to serve (optional)

steps: Pulse the chestnuts in a food processor until roughly chopped.
Add the basil, parsley, mint, parmesan and garlic cloves; pulse again until finely chopped but still textured.
Pour in the rapeseed oil and process briefly to a loose, pourable pesto. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Cook the pasta in plenty of boiling salted water according to pack instructions until just al dente.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add the quartered mushrooms with a good pinch of salt and fry for 6-8 minutes until tender and starting to brown — don’t stir constantly, let them get some colour.
Drain the pasta, return it to the hot pan off the heat.
Stir through the chestnut-herb pesto and the fried mushrooms until every strand is coated.
Serve immediately with extra parmesan on top if you like.

pro_tips: Save a cup of pasta water before draining — if the pesto seems to cling in clumps, a splash of the starchy water emulsifies it into a silky coating.

Buy vacuum-packed cooked chestnuts (supermarkets stock them in October) rather than raw ones — raw chestnuts need the spiky-top boiling or oven-shard treatment to crack open, and the flavour payoff is minimal for a pesto where they get blitzed anyway.
